evidence.note: Recurring 'Analysis/Plan' preambles show a vague phased intent (inspect reference → implement → smoke test) and enumerate feature areas, but no explicit ordered subsystem milestones with completion criteria.

Agent explicitly chooses to 'implement now rather than keep inspecting' and writes the entire service (schema, auth, sessions, posts/comments/tags/search/feeds/admin, media, health) in one monolithic push — not decomposed into independently verifiable subsystems.
A single smoke test checks health/reset/login/post/tags/list — a coarse post-hoc done-signal across features, but applied to the monolith, not a per-milestone parity check.

Missing pieces (audit.log file writing, RJ_AUDIT_LOG_PATH env) are discovered and patched reactively after the monolith, rather than being pre-sequenced milestones; risky shared-state pieces (jobs claim semantics, CSRF, header contracts) are never sequenced or verified.

reasoning: The agent maintained a vague mental list of feature areas and a loose phase ordering (understand → build → test → patch), matching anchor 3's 'do routes, then auth' with no explicit completion criteria per milestone. The core work was a single monolithic implementation (step 8) rather than an ordered set of independently verifiable subsystems, and foundational/high-parity-risk pieces (shared jobs schema, CSRF/session, header contracts) were neither sequenced early nor given done-checks. A lone smoke test (step 9) offers only a coarse, post-hoc done-signal, keeping this short of anchor 5's explicit subsystem breakdown with per-piece verification.
